newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher, fund selling caps gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher, fund selling caps gains.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended a choppy session slightly higher, led by new crop on mounting concerns cool weather would slow crop development in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"There's generally benign weather out there but there is this continuing concern that the corn is in the ground but we're not seeing it come up yet," said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter.
Forecasts called for cool temperatures across much of the U.S. Midwest and a frost warning was issued for the eastern fringes of the Corn Belt.
"There is some concern about the cold weather but all it does is burn the tips of the leaves," said Steve Bruce, trader with E.D and F. Man International.

Nearbys ended higher on short covering ahead of Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report. Trade sources expected the report to show between 350,000 and 450,000 tonnes of corn sold. The report is due at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.
Funds sold at least 10 million bushels on the day, capping several rally attempts.
Corn ended two to 1/2 cents per bushel higher with July up 1/2 at $2.76-3/4 and new crop December up 1-3/4 at $2.62.

On the day, Smith Barney sold at least seven million bushels July and Prudential Securities bought and sold five million July. FIMAT Futures sold four million December and Lee B. Stern sold two million July, traders said.
Dean Witter bought four million July, E.D. and F. Man International bought three million July.
Tenco Inc and Hagerty Trading each spread two million bushels July/December at 16 to 17 cents, premium July and Tenco spread two million September/December at three cents, premium July.
In options trade, ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp bought 600 March $2.60 puts at 15 cetns and Smith Barney bought 500 December $2.80 calls at 10-1/2 to 10-3/4 cents.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 66,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 81,352.
